svgai.marketing.faq_description: A few things to know before you make your first vector.
svgai.marketing.faq_input_question: Can I create an SVG from text or an image?
svgai.marketing.faq_input_answer: Yes. Text to SVG turns a written idea into vector artwork when AI generation is available. Image to SVG traces an existing PNG, JPG, or WebP into vector paths. You can also explore the sample artwork right away.
svgai.marketing.faq_paths_question: Are these real vectors or images inside an SVG?
svgai.marketing.faq_paths_answer: The output contains vector shapes and paths, rather than a raster image placed inside an SVG file. You can scale the artwork and edit its colors in a compatible vector editor.
svgai.marketing.faq_formats_question: Which image formats can I use?
svgai.marketing.faq_formats_answer: Upload a PNG, JPG, or WebP image up to 10 MB. Clear logos, illustrations, and high-contrast artwork make the best starting points. Download your result as an SVG file.
svgai.marketing.faq_privacy_question: Do you upload my image to a server?
svgai.marketing.faq_privacy_answer: No. Image tracing runs locally in your browser, so the image you choose stays on your device. Text prompts are sent to the AI service when text generation is enabled.
svgai.marketing.faq_tools_question: Where can I use the SVG files?
svgai.marketing.faq_tools_answer: Open your SVG in tools such as Figma, Illustrator, or Inkscape, or use it directly on a website. For cutting or embroidery software, check the paths and the file requirements in your chosen tool first.
